name: Tirzepatide
used_for: FDA-labeled for type 2 diabetes glycemic control and cardiovascular risk reduction in adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk (Mounjaro), and for chronic weight management and moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity (Zepbound), alongside diet and activity changes.

entries.text: Zepbound: labeled starting dose 2.5 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 4 weeks, then 5 mg weekly, with increases in 2.5 mg steps every 4 weeks; labeled maintenance dosages are 5, 10 or 15 mg weekly for weight reduction and 10 or 15 mg weekly for obstructive sleep apnea (maximum 15 mg weekly).
entries.population: Adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition; adults with obesity and moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea

entries.text: Mounjaro: labeled starting dose 2.5 mg subcutaneously once weekly, increased in 2.5 mg steps after at least 4 weeks on the current dose as needed for glycemic control; labeled maximum 15 mg weekly in adults and 10 mg weekly in pediatric patients.
entries.population: Adults and pediatric patients 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes

administration_guidance.text: The Zepbound label states the drug is given once weekly at any time of day, with or without meals, by subcutaneous injection into the abdomen, thigh, or another permitted site, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Zepbound and Mounjaro labels state that a missed dose is given as soon as possible within 4 days (96 hours), and is skipped if more than 4 days have passed. The weekly day can be changed if the time between two doses is at least 3 days (72 hours).
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Mounjaro label states single-dose pens and vials are refrigerated (2 to 8 C), may be kept unrefrigerated up to 30 C for a total of 21 days, and are not to be frozen or used if frozen. Opened multi-dose vials and KwikPens are discarded after 30 days or after 4 weekly doses, even if medicine remains.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Zepbound label states vials require a suitable syringe and a new syringe and needle for each injection, the solution should appear clear and colorless to slightly yellow, and the KwikPen is not recommended for self-administration by people who are visually impaired.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: In the Zepbound label's weight-management trials, nausea occurred in 25 to 29% of participants vs 8% with placebo, diarrhea 19 to 23% vs 8%, constipation 11 to 17% vs 5%, vomiting 8 to 13% vs 2%, and abdominal pain 9 to 10% vs 5%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Zepbound label also lists injection site reactions (6 to 8% vs 2%), fatigue, hypersensitivity reactions (5% vs 3%), dizziness, and hair loss (4 to 5% vs 1%).
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In the Mounjaro label's type 2 diabetes trial pool, nausea occurred in 12 to 18% vs 4% with placebo, diarrhea 12 to 17% vs 9%, decreased appetite 5 to 11% vs 1%, and vomiting 5 to 9% vs 2%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Zepbound and Mounjaro labels carry a boxed warning of thyroid C-cell tumors in rats, with unknown relevance to humans, and a contraindication with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Zepbound label lists warnings for acute gallbladder disease and acute pancreatitis.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: WebMD patient reviews of Mounjaro describe big weight losses for many (some report 30 to 80+ pounds), but about a quarter mention significant stomach side effects, and some report hair loss, fatigue or hospitalization.

The British Heart Foundation's news explainer says a Lilly-funded trial found Mounjaro produced more weight loss than Wegovy (about 20% vs 14%), but cautions the trial was open-label and that heart-protection benefit is not yet shown for tirzepatide.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Zepbound (tirzepatide) injection.
research.finding: Approved for weight reduction and moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Mounjaro (tirzepatide) injection.
research.finding: Approved for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes (adults and children 10 and older) and for reducing cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk.

research.summary: SURMOUNT-1: randomized, double-blind, 72-week trial of tirzepatide 5, 10 or 15 mg weekly versus placebo in adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes (Jastreboff et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: Average weight change was -15.0%, -19.5% and -20.9% with the three doses versus -3.1% with placebo; side effects were mostly gastrointestinal.

research.summary: SURPASS-2: randomized trial comparing weekly tirzepatide with semaglutide 1 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes (N Engl J Med).
research.finding: All tirzepatide doses lowered HbA1c more than semaglutide (up to 2.30 vs 1.86 percentage points) and produced greater weight loss; gastrointestinal effects were most common.
